original_question: Let $A$ be an $n x n$ random matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian (or Rademacher, or Bernoulli) entries, and take any $n$-dimensional vector $b$. Is it possible (conditioned on a high-probability event) to solve the linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy faster than $O(n^omega)$?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.8 ("Solving a random linear system") in §2.4, "The effect of outlying singular values (or eigenvalues)," p. 13. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official wording: it has the same n × n random matrix model, the same listed entry distributions (Gaussian / Rademacher / Bernoulli), an arbitrary n-dimensional right-hand side b, the same high-probability conditioning, the same "high accuracy" goal, and the same faster-than-O(n^ω) runtime threshold. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper situates this specifically inside §2.4 as a random-matrix test case for the broader "small outlying singular values" discussion; that motivation is not explicit in the draft. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
The probability is over the draw of A; b is arbitrary rather than random. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

The phrase "conditioned on a high-probability event" is part of the official statement, but the paper does not quantify that event further in Problem 2.8 itself. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

The phrase "to high accuracy" is also left informal in Problem 2.8; no norm, backward-error notion, or tolerance parameter is specified there. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
For a fully stand-alone version, it helps to make explicit that ω denotes the matrix-multiplication exponent.

Problem 2.8 itself does not fix a computation model, even though nearby Problem 2.7 explicitly asks how the answer depends on the model of computation; so one should not silently add a direct-access or matrix-vector-product assumption that the paper does not state here. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

The ambient field is implicit rather than stated; from the listed distributions, the intended setting is real matrices/vectors. This is an inference from the problem statement, not an extra hypothesis proved separately in the paper. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

The paper names "Bernoulli" separately from "Rademacher" but does not further specify the Bernoulli convention in the quoted problem, so a faithful rewrite should keep that wording rather than impose a sharper convention not supplied there. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let A be an n × n random matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian, Rademacher, or Bernoulli entries, and let b be an arbitrary real n-dimensional vector. Is it possible, conditioned on a high-probability event over the draw of A, to solve the linear system Ax = b to high accuracy faster than O(n^ω), where ω denotes the matrix-multiplication exponent? ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
justification: Section 2.4 first frames a broader question about solving (n,0,l,κ) systems with small outlying singular values, then immediately introduces random matrices as a "natural test-case" and states the random-matrix question separately as Problem 2.8. The paper says this broader problem is "closely related" to Problem 2.8, not equivalent to it, so the paper-faithful target is the narrower official Problem 2.8 itself rather than the broader neighboring Problem 2.7. Your draft already matches that official problem almost verbatim; the only sharpening needed is to make the probability source explicit and to avoid adding extra model assumptions not present in the paper. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))
